intro.say: Dinosaurs lived a very long time ago. Let's meet some of them!

rounds.say: Dinosaurs lived long, long ago, before any people. Today we only find their bones in the ground.
rounds.caption: Dinosaurs lived long ago

rounds.say: Some dinosaurs had long necks and ate plants. Some, like T. rex, had big sharp teeth and ate meat.
rounds.caption: Plant eater · Meat eater

rounds.ask: Which dinosaur had a long neck and ate plants?

options.label: T. rex
options.why: T. rex ate meat.

rounds.explain: Long-necked dinosaurs stretched up high to eat leaves from trees.

rounds.ask: Which dinosaur had big sharp teeth for eating meat?

options.label: Long neck
options.why: Long necks ate plants.

rounds.explain: T. rex had huge sharp teeth for eating meat.

rounds.ask: What did baby dinosaurs hatch from?

options.label: A flower
options.why: Flowers don't have dinosaurs in them!

options.label: An apple
options.why: Apples grow on trees.

rounds.explain: Baby dinosaurs hatched out of eggs.

rounds.ask: Can you see a real living dinosaur at the zoo today?

options.label: Yes
options.why: Dinosaurs died out long ago. Zoo dinosaurs are only models!

rounds.explain: Dinosaurs lived long ago. Now we only find their bones.

rounds.ask: What did the long-neck dinosaur eat?

options.label: Meat
options.why: Long-neck dinosaurs were plant eaters.

options.label: Fish
options.why: They ate plants, not fish.

rounds.explain: Long-necked dinosaurs ate leaves and plants.

intro.say: How do we know about dinosaurs? From fossils! Let's be fossil hunters.

rounds.say: A fossil is what is left of a very old plant or animal, turned into stone. Bones, teeth, footprints and shells can become fossils.
rounds.caption: Fossils: very old remains in rock

rounds.say: Fossil hunters dig very carefully. They use small hammers and brushes to clean the rock away from the bones.
rounds.caption: Dig and brush gently

rounds.ask: Which of these could be a fossil?

options.label: Teddy
options.why: A teddy is a toy from today.

options.label: Phone
options.why: Phones are new, not millions of years old.

rounds.explain: Very old bones in rock can be fossils.

rounds.ask: Where do fossil hunters find fossils?

options.label: In clouds
options.why: Fossils are found in the ground.

options.label: In shops
options.why: Fossils come from the ground first.

rounds.explain: Fossils are found buried in rock.

rounds.ask: How does a dinosaur bone become a fossil? Put the steps in order.
rounds.explain: Mud covers the bones, they slowly turn to stone, and millions of years later we dig them up.
rounds.hint: First the dinosaur dies. Last, we find it.

rounds.explain: Plant eaters munched ferns and leaves. Meat eaters ate other animals.

rounds.ask: Why do fossil hunters use soft brushes?

options.label: To paint them
options.why: They clean them, not paint them.

options.label: To sweep the house
options.why: They are cleaning fossils, not the house.

rounds.explain: Old fossils can break, so hunters brush them gently.

intro.say: Fossils are clues. Let's use them like detectives, and find out what happened to the dinosaurs!

rounds.say: Dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago. Scientists think a giant space rock crashed into Earth and changed the weather.
rounds.caption: 66 million years ago

rounds.say: People came millions of years after the dinosaurs, so no person ever saw one. But birds are related to dinosaurs. They are their living cousins!
rounds.caption: Birds are dinosaur cousins

rounds.ask: Which animal alive today is related to the dinosaurs?

options.label: Dog
options.why: Dogs are mammals, not dinosaur cousins.

options.label: Fish
options.why: Fish are a very different group.

rounds.explain: Birds, like chickens, are related to the dinosaurs.

rounds.ask: Did cave people ride on dinosaurs?

options.label: Yes
options.why: That only happens in cartoons! People came millions of years later.

rounds.explain: Dinosaurs died out millions of years before the first people.

rounds.ask: A fossil skull has long, sharp, pointy teeth. What did this dinosaur eat?

options.label: Plants
options.why: Plant eaters had flatter teeth for chewing leaves.

options.label: Honey
options.why: Dinosaurs didn't eat honey!

rounds.explain: Sharp pointy teeth are for biting meat.

rounds.ask: Fossil footprints are huge and very deep in the rock. What do they tell us?

options.label: It was tiny
options.why: Tiny animals leave tiny prints.

options.label: It could fly
options.why: Footprints show walking, not flying.

rounds.explain: Big, deep footprints mean a big, heavy dinosaur pressed into the mud.

rounds.ask: How do we know what dinosaurs looked like?

options.label: Old photos
options.why: There were no cameras back then.

options.label: People saw them
options.why: No person ever saw a living dinosaur.

rounds.explain: Scientists study fossil bones to work out what dinosaurs looked like.

rounds.ask: Put these in order, from longest ago to now.
rounds.explain: Dinosaurs came first, then the space rock, then much later people, and then us today.
